title: Chapter 43: The Allure 1
content:
Chapter 43

Wei Wuxian hadn’t actually expected Lan Wangji to indulge him; he simply tipped his head back and downed the drink himself. To his utter surprise, Lan Wangji watched him in silence for a few beats, then gathered his wide sleeve with a graceful tuck, reached out, and poured a cup of his own. Pausing for just a second, he lifted the cup to his lips and drained it slowly.

A spark of amused wonder lit up Wei Wuxian’s eyes. "Hanguang-jun, aren't you a sweetheart? You're really having a drink with me?"

Last time around, Wei Wuxian hadn't paid close enough attention to the man's expressions, but tonight he was watching like a hawk.

Lan Wangji drank with his eyes closed, his brows knitting into a faint, delicate pinch. The moment the cup emptied, his lips pressed together in a subtle, fleeting purse before his lashes lifted. When his pale eyes opened, a soft, glassy shimmer lingered across his irises.

Wei Wuxian propped his chin in his hand, quietly counting the seconds in his head. Right on schedule—the moment he hit eight—Lan Wangji set the cup down, rested his forehead in his hand, and closed his eyes. Out cold, just like that.

Wei Wuxian shook his head in sheer, helpless admiration: the man really did pass out before he got drunk.

A sudden urge to cause trouble flared up in his chest. Tipping the last drops of the wine jar into his mouth, he stood up, hands tucked behind his back, and took a leisurely lap around the private booth. Slipping up beside Lan Wangji, he leaned down and murmured right into his ear, "Lan Zhan?"

Not a peep. Wei Wuxian prodded again, "Wangji-xiong?"

Lan Wangji remained still, forehead cradled in his right hand, his breathing slow, steady, and tranquil.

Bathed in the soft light, his face and long, slender fingers were pristine, pale as polished mutton-fat jade.

The faint sandalwood scent drifting off his skin had always carried a solitary, frosty chill. But blended with the rich, mellow fragrance of warm liquor, that cool incense took on a cozy, sweet, heady note that made the air feel dangerously intoxicating.

Hovering this close, the fragrance wrapped around Wei Wuxian’s senses. Without realizing it, he leaned in further, closing the gap until he caught himself wondering in a haze:Weird... why does it feel so warm in here?

Drunk on wine fumes and cold sandalwood, his face crept nearer and nearer. His voice dropped into a low, playful purr, whispering against the shell of the sleeping man's ear: "Lan-er... ge..."

Out of the blue, a faint, disembodied whisper ghosted through the room: "Gongzi..."

Wei Wuxian’s nose was practically brushing Lan Wangji’s cheek, the lingering "gege" teetering right on the edge of his tongue. The voice snapped him out of his daze so violently his boot slid on the floorboards, nearly taking a spill right over the table.

In a flash of pure instinct, he stepped back to shield Lan Wangji behind him, whirling around to face the wooden window where the sound had come from.

A tentative tap rattled against the slats, followed by that same timid whisper filtering through the seams: "Gongzi..."

Only then did Wei Wuxian realize his heart was hammering against his ribs at an absurd clip. Cursing his own jumpiness, he steadied his breath, strode over, and shoved the shutters open. Clinging to the overhanging eaves outside was a dark, spindly figure hanging upside down like a bat, knuckles raised to knock again. Caught off guard by the sudden swing of the shutter, the wooden frame clipped him squarely on the crown. He let out a muffled yelp, catching the swinging window with both hands, coming face-to-face with Wei Wuxian.

A draft of crisp night air rushed into the room. Wen Ning blinked at him, the lifeless, pupilless white of his eyes replaced by a pair of quiet, obsidian-dark irises.

The two of them froze—one standing tall, the other dangling by his ankles—staring at each other in stunned silence.

Wei Wuxian cleared his throat. "Get down."

Wen Ning’s ankles lost their purchase on the eaves. With a dull thud, he plummeted straight down, crashing hard into the dirt below.

Wei Wuxian wiped a nonexistent bead of cold sweat from his brow.

Bless this tavern,he thought.

Booking this particular room had been a stroke of genius. To ensure quiet, the window didn't overlook the bustling thoroughfare; it faced a secluded grove of bamboo and shade trees. Wei Wuxian propped the shutters open with a wooden dowel, leaned his torso over the sill, and peeked down. Wen Ning’s fierce corpse bulk was ridiculously dense—he had carved a human-shaped crater right into the soil. He was still sprawled flat in the dent, looking up with wide, blinking eyes.

Wei Wuxian hissed down in a harsh whisper, "I told you to get downhere, not plunge to the ground! 'Down,' as in come inside! Are you dense?"

Wen Ning craned his neck, scrambled out of the dirt crater, and brushed off his ragged robes. "Oh," he mumbled hastily. "I'm coming."

Wrapping his arms around a support pillar, he braced to shimmy his way back up the wall. Wei Wuxian cut him off: "Hold it! Stay right where you are. I'll come down to you."

He slipped back over to Lan Wangji’s side, leaning close to his ear: "Lan Zhan, my good man, do me a favor and sleep like a log, alright? I’ll be back in a flash. Be good, okay?"

Pulling back, his fingers twitched with a sudden itch. Unable to help himself, he reached out and gently flicked the tips of Lan Wangji’s long eyelashes.

The light tease made Lan Wangji’s lashes flutter softly, his brow knitting into a faint, restless pinch. Pulling his hand back like he’d been burned, Wei Wuxian vaulted out the window, skipping across the eaves and dipping branches before landing soundlessly on the turf below.

The moment he turned around, Wen Ning dropped heavily to his knees.

Wei Wuxian sighed. "What on earth are you doing?"

Wen Ning kept his chin pinned to his collarbone, not breathing a word.

"Do we really have to talk like this?" Wei Wuxian asked.

Wen Ning kept his voice low, thick with misery: "Gongzi, I'm sorry."

Wei Wuxian clicked his tongue. "Fine."

With a rustle of fabric, he dropped to his knees right in front of him. Wen Ning flinched in horror, hastily pressing his forehead to the dirt in a desperate kowtow. Without missing a beat, Wei Wuxian dropped his own forehead to the ground, matching him stroke for stroke. Terrified out of his wits, Wen Ning scrambled to his feet. Only then did Wei Wuxian push himself upright, dusting the gravel from his hems.

"See? Isn't it much nicer to talk with your spine straight?"

Wen Ning ducked his head, terrified to make a sound.

"When did your head clear?" Wei Wuxian asked.

"Just now."

"Do you remember anything while those cranial spikes were shoved into your skull?"

Wen Ning frowned. "Bits and pieces... most of it is gone."

"What do you remember?"

"I remember... being bound in heavy iron chains in the dark. Every now and then, someone would come to check on me."

"Did you catch their face?"

"No," Wen Ning murmured. "I only remember someone driving spikes deep into my skull."

"Xue Yang, most likely," Wei Wuxian reasoned. "He used the exact same cranial nails to puppet Song Lan. He used to be a guest cultivator for Lanling Jin; what I can't pin down is whether he acted on his own or on their orders." He paused, rubbing his chin before shaking his head. "No, it had to be Lanling Jin. Back then, they announced to the world that your bones had been burned to ash and scattered. Without the Jin clan pulling strings from the shadows, a lone rogue could never pull off a cover-up that massive."

He looked at him. "What happened after that? How did you end up on Dafan Mountain?"

Wen Ning hesitated. "After that... I don't know how much time passed. Suddenly, I heard two sharp claps, and Gongzi’s voice shouting,'Wake up!'So I... I tore through the chains and broke out..."

The command at the Mo estate.The order he had snapped at those three fresh corpses in the parlor.

Back in his prime, the Yiling Laozu had drilled countless commands into the Ghost General. Naturally, the very first order Wei Wuxian loosed upon returning to the living world had resonated through the spiritual tether, waking Wen Ning from his slumber.

Trapped in a fog of instinct, Wen Ning had followed the trail of dark energy and Wei Wuxian's summons across the countryside. Meanwhile, the Lanling Jin Sect knew that harboring the Ghost General was a political powder keg; if word leaked, the fallout would not only ruin their reputation but trigger absolute panic across the clans. Even after Wen Ning broke loose, they didn't dare launch a public manhunt, leaving their search parties crippled by secrecy. Wandering blindly, Wen Ning had finally caught the frantic whistle of a crude bamboo flute on Dafan Mountain, homing in on the call.

Wei Wuxian let out a low sigh. "Your 'I don't know how much time' was over a decade."

He paused, softening his tone. "Though, I suppose I'm in the same boat. Want me to catch you up on what happened while we were gone?"

Wen Ning murmured, "I've heard some of it."

"Oh? What did you hear?"

"I heard... the Burial Mounds fell. Everyone... is gone."

Wei Wuxian had planned to toss out a few harmless, absurd tidbits—like how the Lan clan's stone wall of rules had ballooned from three thousand lines to over four thousand—hoping to lighten the mood. Hearing Wen Ning drop that lead weight into the conversation made his throat lock up.

Yet heavy as the words were, Wen Ning’s voice wasn't choked with weeping; it sounded like an acceptance of an inevitability he had braced for long ago. And truly, they had. Thirteen years ago, the worst possible ending had been calculated and recalculated hundreds of times.

After a long silence, Wei Wuxian asked softly, "What else did you hear?"

"Sect Leader Jiang Cheng led the siege," Wen Ning whispered. "He killed you."

Wei Wuxian shook his head. "Let me clear that up: he didn't land the killing blow. My own craft backfired and tore me apart."

Wen Ning lifted his head, his dark eyes locking onto Wei Wuxian's. "Still, Sect Leader Jiang... he clearly..."

"No one gets to walk a single-plank bridge in the dark forever without taking a spill," Wei Wuxian cut in gently. "It couldn't be helped."

Wen Ning looked as though he wanted to sigh, but lacking breath, the motion died in his chest.

"Alright, that's enough about him," Wei Wuxian said, waving it off. "Anything else you picked up?"

"Yes." Wen Ning stared at him with profound sorrow. "Wei-gongzi... you died a terrible death."

Wei Wuxian rubbed his nose, thoroughly exasperated by the puppy-dog grief. "Good grief, did you not catch a single piece of good news?"

Wen Ning’s brow furrowed in earnest distress. "No. Not a single word."

Wei Wuxian was entirely at a loss for words.

Just then, the sharp shatter of breaking porcelain echoed from the tavern’s ground floor. Lan Sizhui’s panicked voice cut through the clamor: "Weren't we just discussing Xue Yang? How did we get dragged into an argument over this?!"

Jin Ling’s furious snarl tore through the slats: "Weweretalking about Xue Yang, and what I said wasn't wrong! What kind of monster was Xue Yang? A subhuman piece of garbage! And Wei Ying was ten times more revolting than him! What do you mean 'we can't lump them together'?! Scum who walk the crooked path are a blight on this earth—every last one of them should be slaughtered, wiped out, eradicated!"

Wen Ning shifted, his posture stiffening, but Wei Wuxian held up a flat hand, signaling him to freeze.

Lan Jingyi’s indignant holler chimed in: "What are you throwing a tantrum for?! Sizhui never said Wei Wuxian didn't deserve to die! He just said not everyone who cultivates the dark path is a butcher like Xue Yang! Did you really have to smash a plate? I hadn't even finished eating that..."

Jin Ling let out a venomous scoff. "Didn't he also say that'perhaps the founder never intended for the craft to be used for evil'?! And who is that 'founder'? Go on, tell me—who else could it be besides Wei Ying?! It’s sickening! Your Gusu Lan Sect is supposed to be a premier, righteous clan, and plenty of your own disciples died by Wei Ying’s hands back then! Did you forget the blood spilled hacking through his walking corpses and ghouls? Why the hell are you defending him, Lan Yuan?! From the way you're talking, you sound like you're trying to make excuses for the monster!"

Lan Yuan was Sizhui's courtesy name. He pushed back, his tone steady despite the heat: "I am not making excuses for anyone. I am merely suggesting that before we understand the full picture, we should not rush to pass judgment. Before we entered Yi City, didn't half the world swear that Chang Ping of Yueyang was butchered by Daozhang Xiao Xingchen out of bitter vengeance? And what was the truth?"

Jin Ling snapped, "Nobody laid eyes on Chang Ping’s murder! That was gossip and speculation, not verified fact! But what about the ambush at Qiongqi Path? What about the bloodbath at Nightless City?! In those two battles, how many cultivators lost their lives to his sorcery, to Wen Ning, and to the Yin Tiger Tally?! Thousands watched it happen with their own two eyes! You can't twist that, you can't deny it! And he sicced Wen Ning on my father to kill him, and got my mother murdered—do you think I could ever forget that?!"

If Wen Ning had a drop of living blood in his veins, his face would have drained bone-white.

His voice shook: "...Lady Jiang's son?"

Wei Wuxian stood frozen, unmoving as stone.

Jin Ling's voice grew louder, thick with jagged grief: "My uncle grew up alongside him! My grandfather treated him like his own flesh and blood, and my grandmother was good to him too! And how did he repay them?! He dragged Lotus Pier down until it became a filthy den for the Wen dogs, shattered the Yunmeng Jiang clan into splinters, and got both my grandparents and my parents killed, leaving my uncle all alone in this world! He brought every bit of that karma down on his own head, died without a whole corpse left to bury! What 'full picture' is there to unravel?! What excuse could you possibly make for him?!"

The boy's words were barbed arrows, leaving Lan Sizhui in stunned, breathless silence. After a heavy beat, another gentle voice piped up, trying to defuse the room: "Come on, why are we ruining a good meal over this? Can we drop it? The food's getting cold."

It was the romantic disciple Wei Wuxian had teased earlier, Ouyang Zizhen. Another boy chimed in: "Zizhen is right, stop fighting. Sizhui just spoke without thinking; he didn't mean anything by it. Young Master Jin, sit back down, let's eat."

"Yeah, we just survived Yi City together; we’re practically brothers-in-arms now... Why let careless words ruin the night?"

Jin Ling huffed a sharp breath. Sizhui smoothed his robes, his tone returning to its trademark, polite composure: "My apologies. I spoke thoughtlessly and overstepped. Young Master Jin, please, take a seat. If this noise draws Hanguang-jun downstairs, none of us will hear the end of it."

Throwing Hanguang-jun's name into the ring worked like a charm; Jin Ling swallowed his retort, the scuffling of stools signaling that everyone was settling back into their seats. The lively tavern chatter rushed in to fill the silence, the juniors' voices drowning beneath the clatter of porcelain and clinking cups.

Yet out in the dark grove, Wei Wuxian and Wen Ning remained motionless, their faces locked in heavy, suffocating silence.

Without a sound, Wen Ning sank back onto both knees. It took Wei Wuxian several seconds to notice. He waved a tired hand. "It wasn't your fault."

Wen Ning opened his mouth to reply, but his gaze suddenly drifted past Wei Wuxian's shoulder, freezing in place. Before Wei Wuxian could turn around, a flash of white robes swept past him, and a pristine boot slammed squarely into Wen Ning’s chest.

The impact sent Wen Ning skidding backward, plowing a second human-shaped trench into the mud.

Wei Wuxian scrambled forward, throwing his arms around Lan Wangji to hold him back. "Hanguang-jun! Hanguang-jun, mercy! Calm down!"

The nap was clearly over; the drunk phase had begun. Lan Wangji had hunted him down.

The situation was absurdly familiar—history repeating itself down to the letter. Except this time, Lan Wangji looked remarkably put-together. His boots were on the correct feet, his robes were immaculate, and even while booting a fierce corpse into the dirt, his face remained so stern, righteous, and noble that you couldn't find a single flaw in his posture. Held back by Wei Wuxian, he snapped his wide sleeves, gave a stiff nod of acknowledgment, and stood planted like an unyielding pine, obediently holding his fire.

Wei Wuxian stole a glance down into the ditch. "You alright?"

Wen Ning sat up, coughing dust. "I'm fine."

"Then get up! What are you still kneeling for?"

Wen Ning scrambled out of the mud, hesitated for a beat, and murmured, "Lan-gongzi."

Lan Wangji’s brow pinched. Clamping both hands tightly over his ears, he pivoted sharply on his heel, turning his back entirely to Wen Ning and stepping right in front of Wei Wuxian, using his broad shoulders to physically block him from view.

Wen Ning stood there, completely lost.

Wei Wuxian chuckled dryly. "You'd better clear out. Lan Zhan... well, he's not exactly thrilled to see you."

Wen Ning blinked. "...What happened to Lan-gongzi?"

"Nothing major," Wei Wuxian said breezily. "Just drunk."

"Ah?" Wen Ning’s jaw went slack, looking utterly incapable of processing that concept. After an agonizing silence, he managed, "Then... what should we do?"

"What else can I do? I'll drag him back inside and toss him into bed."

Lan Wangji chimed in flatly, "Good."

Wei Wuxian sputtered, "Wait, aren't your ears covered?! How the hell did you hear that?!"

This time, Lan Wangji offered no reply, hands still clamped firmly over his ears, acting for all the world as if he hadn't just spoken. Wei Wuxian didn't know whether to laugh or cry. Turning back to Wen Ning, he softened his tone: "Look after yourself out there."

Wen Ning nodded, casting one last bewildered look at Lan Wangji. Just as he turned to leave, Wei Wuxian called him back: "Wen Ning. Maybe... find somewhere quiet to lay low for a while."

Wen Ning paused.

Wei Wuxian sighed softly. "You’ve died twice already. Get some rest."

Once the dark silhouette vanished into the trees, Wei Wuxian reached up and gently pried Lan Wangji’s hands away from his head. "Alright, he's gone. You can't hear him, and you can't see him."

Lan Wangji lowered his hands, those pale, glass-clear eyes staring straight into Wei Wuxian's face with deadpan intensity.

The gaze was so earnest, so pure, that a devilish spark of mischief detonated inside Wei Wuxian’s chest. His blood buzzed with a sudden, wicked urge to cause chaos. Leaning in with an impish grin, he tested, "Lan Zhan, are we playing the game where you answer whatever I ask, and do whatever I say?"

Lan Wangji nodded. "Mm."

"Take off your forehead ribbon."

Without a second thought, Lan Wangji reached behind his head, untied the silken knot, and slipped the cloud-patterned white ribbon from his brow.

Wei Wuxian took the ribbon into his palms, turning it over and over, inspecting the fine embroidery. "Doesn't look like anything special. Here I thought it held some earth-shattering secret. Why did you get so furious when I snatched it off you back in the day?"Did the teenage Lan Wangji simply hate my guts that much?

Before he could finish the thought, a sudden tug cinched his wrists tight.

Lan Wangji was wrapping the ribbon around both of his hands, meticulously tying a knot.

Wei Wuxian blinked. "What are you doing?"

Curious to see what the drunkard was playing at, he didn't resist. Lan Wangji bound his wrists snugly together, looped a slipknot, paused to evaluate it, decided it wasn't secure enough, untied it, and cinched it into a firm square knot. He evaluated it again, still dissatisfied, and added another.

The ribbons of the Gusu Lan Sect had long trailing tails meant to flutter with regal elegance, leaving plenty of slack. Lan Wangji tied seven or eight stubborn knots in a row, creating a thick, ugly cluster of silk, before stepping back with a satisfied nod.

Wei Wuxian held up his bound hands. "Hey, do you even want this ribbon back?"

Lan Wangji’s brow smoothed over. Gripping the trailing end of the silk like a leash, he hauled Wei Wuxian’s wrists up to eye level, admiring his handiwork like a proud artisan. Dangling from the ribbon, Wei Wuxian frowned.I look like a damn prisoner... Wait, why am I playing along? Wasn't I supposed to be the one messing with him?

Snapping back to reality, Wei Wuxian tugged. "Untie me."

Lan Wangji leaned forward, hands darting toward Wei Wuxian's collar and waist sash.

"Not those clothes!" Wei Wuxian yelped, leaning back. "Untie my hands! Untie this ribbon you just bound me with!"

Getting stripped naked while hogtied by Lan Wangji was a nightmare scenario he wasn't about to risk living through.

Hearing the correction, Lan Wangji’s brow furrowed into a tight knot, standing motionless for a long time. Wei Wuxian thrust his bound wrists forward, coaxing him like a child: "Didn't you say you'd do whatever I asked? Untie your gege's hands, there's a good boy."

Lan Wangji looked at him, then calmly looked away into the distance, putting on a show of intense, profound contemplation.

Wei Wuxian groaned. "Oh, I see how it is! Tell you to tie me up and you're all over it; tell you to untie me and suddenly you don't speak the language?!"

The silk used for the Lan Sect ribbons matched their robes—ethereal and airy to the touch, but spun with tensile spiritual threads that made it virtually unbreakable. With Lan Wangji’s tight series of knots, Wei Wuxian’s twisting did nothing to loosen the cinch.Talk about shooting yourself in the foot,he grumbled inwardly.Good thing it's just a ribbon and not a Deity-Binding Cord, or he’d have trussed me up like a prize pig.

Lan Wangji continued staring into the distance, idly tugging and swaying the ribbon tether like a toddler playing with a pet.

Wei Wuxian sighed, putting on his most pathetic whine: "Come on, untie me, please? Hanguang-jun, an immortal beauty like you shouldn't be playing kidnapper. What if someone sees us like this? How bad would that look?"

At the word "sees," Lan Wangji gave the ribbon a firm yank, dragging him straight toward the tree line.

Stumbling behind him, Wei Wuxian yelped, "Wait, wait, wait! I meant it looks bad if people see us, not 'let's go parade this around in public'! Hey! Are you faking this?! You're doing this on purpose, aren't you?! You only hear what you want to hear! Lan Zhan! Lan Wangji!"

Before he could finish his tirade, Lan Wangji had dragged him clear out of the grove, looped around the street, and marched straight through the tavern’s front doors.

Down in the dining hall, the disciples were halfway through a lively drinking game, the earlier tension long forgotten with the resilience of youth. A few daring Lan boys had even snuck a flask onto the table, keeping an eye glued to the stairs to watch for Hanguang-jun. Nobody on earth expected Lan Wangji to stroll through the main entrance dragging a tethered Wei Wuxian behind him.

Every single head whipped around, freezing mid-laugh.

A chaotic clatter erupted as Lan Jingyi lunged across the table to hide the wine cup, knocking over three side dishes in the scramble—failing to conceal a thing and drawing maximum attention to the contraband.

Lan Sizhui scrambled to his feet, stammering, "H-Hanguang-jun, how did you... why are you coming from outside...?"

Wei Wuxian forced a loud, boisterous laugh: "Haha! Your Hanguang-jun was feeling warm upstairs, so he stepped out for a stroll! Lo and behold, a surprise inspection caught you little rascals sneaking booze!"

Internally, he was praying to every deity he knew:Lan Zhan, please, just drag me upstairs. Don't speak, don't move, just keep that cold, deadpan face on and nobody will notice you're blitzed.

Right on cue, Lan Wangji tugged the ribbon, leading Wei Wuxian straight up to the disciples' table.

Lan Sizhui gasped, "Hanguang-jun, your forehead ribbon..."

The words died in his throat. His gaze had dropped to Wei Wuxian's wrists.

There it was: Hanguang-jun's sacred ribbon, cinched tight around Wei Wuxian's hands.

And as if worried the room hadn't gotten a clear enough look, Lan Wangji gave the ribbon a deliberate pull, lifting Wei Wuxian's bound hands high into the air for everyone to see.
